newsitem.title: THAILAND: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - Oct 29.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - Oct 29.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Thai press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Five Israelis have been seriously injured in a cable car accident in the northern province of Chiang Mai. The car carrying 20 tourists derailed and crashed after the cable snapped halfway up Doi Suthep yesterday. (BANGKOK POST)

- Queen Elizabeth II renewed her acquaintance with Thailand again after 24 years yesterday. The British monarch and the Duke of Edinburgh, her consort, who are on a five-day state visit, were greeted at Don Muang Airport by Their Majesties the King and Queen. (BANGKOK POST) (THE NATION)

- The New Aspiration Party has named Amnuay Viravan as a key member of its economic team and Thanong Bidaya, president of Thai Military Bank, as his economic adviser. But signs of a rift have emerged within the party when leader Chavalit Yongchaiyudh and secretary-general Snoh Thienthong went on separate campaign trails amid reports of conflicts over pro-Chavalit rally schedules. (THE NATION)

- An arrest warrant has been issued for property developer Prasong Panitpakdee, chairman and managing director of Somprasong Land Plc, on charges of doctoring financial statements, causing the company's share prices to fall heavily. The warrant was issued after police received complaints from the company's shareholders. (MANAGER) (KRUNG THEP THURAKIJ)

- The Bank of Thailand expects to introduce a new tool by the end of the year to help it manage the money market more effectively. Known as open market operation, the system will make the central bank an active player in the money market through bond trading with local financial institutions selected as direct dealers. (BANGKOK POST)

- Outgoing Deputy Prime Minister Amnuay Viravan has lashed out at the Port Authority of Thailand's (PAT) recent attempt to extend the trucking monopoly inside Bangkok Port to the state-run Express Transportation Organisation (ETO), saying that the former must abide by the Cabinet policy to liberalise the business. The attempted move by the PAT to renew the ETO trucking monopoly for another two years has also come under strong criticism from exporters. (THE NATION)
